visual_fidelity_confidence: CSS-inferred only. No rendered screenshots, Storybook build output, or visual-regression artifacts exist anywhere in the run, so fidelity was assessed by comparing declared token/CSS values (palette, spacing, radii, shadow) against several reference screenshots (screen.png, screen_2.png, screen_4.png) rather than against actual rendered pixels.

findings.summary: Every responsive layout in the run is desktop-first, not mobile-first: base (unqueried) rules define multi-column desktop grids and a `@media (max-width: Npx)` override collapses to a single column. All 6 media-query sites in the run use max-width exclusively; none use min-width/progressive enhancement from a mobile base.

All component/template CSS modules consistently reference CSS custom properties (var(--color-x), var(--space-x), etc.), but the values behind those custom properties are hand-duplicated literals in design-system/src/styles.css rather than being produced from the DTCG/Theme pipeline (the resolver that would do this, resolveTokens.mjs, is unused dead code). Styling therefore does not actually adhere to the profile-selected token pipeline; it adheres to a parallel hardcoded copy of it.

No viewport/responsive-inspection addon is configured in Storybook (.storybook/main.ts declares addons: []), so the six responsive breakpoints implemented in CSS are not conveniently inspectable through any configured tooling in the static documentation surface.

The same "panel/card" visual recipe (border + border-radius + surface background + box-shadow + padding, all via tokens) is independently redeclared in at least three separate template CSS modules instead of being centralized in one shared primitive/base class.
